email.body1:
Hayden, saw Bolt named Affirm its default BNPL across the checkout network as it builds the first federated checkout network.

Momentum like that usually means more in-market merchant accounts than the team can cover, and that is where good-fit deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Bolt off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Hayden, quick follow-up for Bolt.

As the checkout network expands, merchant targets grow faster than your selling capacity can. Most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Bolt needs to cover merchant targets this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Hayden, last bit of proof for Bolt.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Bolt's reply rate likely compares to other commerce and payments infrastructure firms. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a commerce sales motion? I will tailor it to Bolt either way.
